header: Step 2 of the front-path plan (HANDOFF_dsp-intranet_front-path.md): ROUTE LOGGING. It is PASSIVE: it changes no answer, it only records, for every /api/ai-search request, what happened between the Enter key and the reply:
- which route answered (holiday / nl2sql / cache / legacy / clarify / circular / eds / title / none / error),
- how long each stage took (name checks, the omnibar engine, circular search, synthesis),
- how many model calls it made and how many tokens they used, and how long a Groq rate-limit made it wait.

The numbers go out as response headers (x-omni-*, Server-Timing) and as ONE console line per request, so the acceptance harness and the person at the keyboard read the same facts: I want no guessing where the time goes. I use AsyncLocalStorage, so the model adapter (nl2sql/llm.ts) and the synthesis call can report their usage without being passed anything; outside a traced request every function here quietly does nothing (scripts, tests).

members.name: ms
doc: Wall-clock milliseconds of this one call.

members.name: kind
doc: The analytics kind (count, clarify, error ...), when the answer was one.

members.name: gate
doc: What the front-path gate (frontGate.ts) decided: "skipped" (model skipped, circular search first), "model" (asked as before) or "fallback" (it skipped, circular search found nothing or failed, so the model was asked after all). null = the gate is off.

members.name: synth
doc: The synthesis-intent verdict for the question (synthesisIntent.ts), as "level;score", e.g. "synthesis;7". null = not asked.

members.name: plan
doc: What the umbrella's planner (src/records/plan.ts) would have chosen for the line, and the selection the reader made ("auto" when none). This is the shadow comparison. null = not recorded.

members.name: waitedMs
doc: Milliseconds spent sleeping because Groq said "too many tokens this minute".

members.name: tokens
members.type: { prompt: number; completion: number; total: number; cached: number }

symbols.name: startTrace
symbols.sig: export function startTrace(now: number = Date.now()): Trace

symbols.name: withTrace
symbols.sig: export function withTrace<T>(trace: Trace, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>
doc: Runs `fn` with `trace` as the current request's trace; everything it awaits sees it.

symbols.name: traceStep
doc: Start timing a stage and call the returned function to stop. Repeated stages with the same name add up.

symbols.name: setTraceRoute
symbols.sig: export function setTraceRoute(route: string, kind?: string | null): void

symbols.name: setTraceSynth

symbols.name: setTracePlan
symbols.sig: export function setTracePlan(plan: string, scope: string): void

symbols.name: summarizeTrace
symbols.sig: export function summarizeTrace(t: Trace, now: number = Date.now()): TraceSummary

symbols.name: routeFromReply
symbols.sig: export function routeFromReply(status: number, mode: string, body: unknown): { route: string; kind: string | null }
doc: I name the route from the reply itself. The server decided what to send, so the shape of the reply (and the `source` the omnibar engine stamps on an analytics answer) IS the route. A list is circular search; an empty list is "none".

symbols.name: traceHeaders
symbols.sig: export function traceHeaders(s: TraceSummary): Record<string, string>
doc: The headers the harness (and a browser's network tab) can read. All values are plain ASCII, on purpose.

symbols.name: traceLine
symbols.sig: export function traceLine(s: TraceSummary, query: string): string
doc: ONE readable line per request for the server console (dev terminal / Vercel log).

behaviours: no-ops outside a trace do not throw
stopping a step twice counts once
console line mentions a synthesis-type question
console line stays quiet for an ordinary question
console line shortens a long question
console line mentions the rate-limit wait
console line for a free answer
and the time it slept for the 429
console line stays quiet under Everything when the planner has no reading
console line names a chosen selection beside the planner's reading
console line names the planner's reading under Everything
